customize.text:
More than two thousand years ago, a white serpent, Orobashi, fled from the Archon War to the Dark Sea and became a god of the ancient civilization of
During his reign, a secret research institute was established in Byakuyakoku to study the Bathysmal Vishaps, the inhabitants of the Light Realm, and indigenous species to the Dark Sea. They were primordial elemental beings, unbent and unbowed by the power that came from the heavens owing to their living deep underwater. During the war with humans, they evolved into various elemental forms. Under Orobashi's direction, experiments were conducted on the Vishaps to implant corals that grew on Orobashi’s body into them. The researchers lowered the temperature in the habitat of the young heat-resistant Vishaps, and as a result, they were weak when they matured. This may have happened because their bodies did not have the "seed" needed to withstand such an environment. However, their descendants would all possess high body fat, a greater predilection towards sleep, and would express the Cryo element. When placed into sweltering conditions, they, like their ancestors, again chose heat resistance traits, but none of them developed the traits indicative of the Pyro element. It has been suggested that the Vishaps can freely awaken their "seed" before maturation and that Vishap mothers can also create new "seeds" to pass on to their offspring if they encounter heretofore unseen, challenging environments.

Many attempts to transplant Orobasi's corals to the Vishaps were unsuccessful. Since the Vishaps belonged to the Light Realm, they could not accept the blood of the serpent that belonged to the Human Realm, and various negative reactions occurred in their bodies. According to the plans for the evolutionary line of the Vishaps, the experiments were to lead to the creation of the most powerful Vishap of all possible. The results of the intelligence tests showed that the Vishaps always had their own methods of communication, and in the fourth generation after training, they had a linguistic understanding comparable to that of a 12-year-old human student. After improving the intellectual abilities of the Vishaps, the researchers decided to stop the experiments to prevent the Vishaps from evolving into Vishap-people. According to the prophecy, the next Hydro Dragon was to be born in human form. There is a riddle in Enkanomiya: what walks on four feet in the early morning, two feet during the day, and three feet at night? The answer is: A Vishap who transforms into a person to attend a ball, then breaks one of its legs and eventually ends up walking with a cane. Although adults may think that there is a conspiracy here, because a Vishap cannot transform into a human, Dragonheirs of the Depths have evolved to wield the power of other elements and have hence lost their purity. As such, the Dragon of Water could no longer be born from among their ranks. Researchers could not allow the Hydro Sovereign to be born in Enkanomiya, but it was the experiments on the Vishaps that could have caused this prophecy to come true. When all the people left the Dark Sea, they were going to release all the specially improved Bathysmal Vishaps. Their properties were to be passed on to their offspring, and within a few years, a large population of Vishaps was to appear in the area.

customize.text:
The protector of the Erinnyes Forest is an evolved Vishap who ended up in Fontaine. Although she looks like a Melusine, she has never been to Merusea Village, nor the Court of Fontaine, and can take the form of a Primordial Bathysmal Vishap. One day, she met a
— the Hydro Dragon who was born in a human form as the Byakuyakoku prophet foretold. He taught her a human language and entrusted her to protect the island. She learned to say "Melusine" as "no," and "Pahsiv" as "yes," so Paimon named her Pahsiv, which is "Vishap" backwards. All of Erinnyes is the information system of the Hydro Dragon, through which he can sense changes in the water veins. The weeping willow near the lake collected information, the fog processed it, and the Loch Urania spring sent it. When the filth began to destroy the roots of the weeping willow connecting the water veins, Pahsiv turned for help to the Traveler and Paimon, who were passing by. If the willow roots were destroyed by the Root-Consuming Tumor, the information system would fail to function, and Neuvillette's senses would be affected.

To save the weeping willow, Pahsiv, the Traveler, and Paimon sought three teardrop keys that opened a secret passage in the roots of the Erinnyes. To obtain the key on the foggy path in the south of the island, they returned three drops of pure dew to the glowing tree. The key near the willow on the east of the island was hidden near an altar underwater, trapped by seaweed. When Pahsiv, the Traveler, and Paimon went to retrieve the third key from a spring in the north, they encountered a Bathysmal Vishap near an activated altar. Taking the Vishap for a threat, the Traveler and Paimon attempted to defend Pahsiv, but she merely patted the Vishap on the head, explaining that the filth had wounded it. Calmed, the Vishap spat out the last key, which it continued to protect even after being wounded.

Once all the keys were collected, Pahsiv, the Traveler, and Paimon went to the square near the Marcotte station, where a fountain with lion sculptures stood. A secret passage beneath this fountain, opened with three keys, led to the heart of the Erinnyes. To help the Traveler cleanse the weeping willow of its taint, Pahsiv shared some of her power with them, enhancing their abilities. During the battle with the filth, Rifthounds suddenly appeared from a magic circle on the ground. Taking the form of a Vishap, Pahsiv helped defeat the Rifthounds, and the tree's roots were completely cleansed. After saving the Erinnyes Forest, Pahsiv, in gratitude, found treasure chests for Paimon and the Traveler, who, in return, promised to visit her, feed her Tidalga, teach her the language, and show her how to say goodbye properly.

When the Melusines, whom Neuvillette treats like his daughters, decided to make him a new suit, Pahsiv quietly followed Puca, who was searching for beautiful stones and shells to decorate the suit. While the Traveler and Paimon were helping collect shells underwater, Puca was attacked by an armored crab, but Pahsiv, transforming into a Vishap, ate the crab and disappeared, leaving the Melusine her favorite Tidalga. When the suit was finished and ceremoniously presented to Neuvillette, they went together to lunch on Beryl Island, where they met Pahsiv again. The Melusines befriended the little Vishap, fed her Tidalga, and gave her a badge depicting Neuvillette.
